notes: Primary source: Kroeze, Kristensen, Pucher, '171Yb Reference Data', arXiv:2509.04416v1 (tables parsed from the arXiv HTML; a v2 exists and was not compared). Entries whose source ends with 'as tabulated in Kroeze...' are that paper's weighted means of the original references named (method 'compilation'); its quoted 'Birge ratio' > 1 means the inputs were mutually inconsistent and the uncertainty was inflated. FREQUENCIES: frequency_THz of the main lines refers to the hyperfine CENTRE OF GRAVITY of 171Yb, not to 174Yb and not to a specific F component; NIST level energies used as identifiers are natural-mixture values, so they differ from the 171Yb numbers at the 0.05 cm^-1 level. ISOTOPE SHIFTS are nu(first) - nu(second); values with "derived": true were computed here as differences of tabulated numbers (formula given in the entry's source) and are not printed in any paper. A_s: for 399, 556, 578 nm it equals 1/lifetime of the upper level (branching ~1). For 649, 770, 1389 nm it is the reference paper's 'partial decay rate' = theoretical branching ratio (from Porsev 1999 E1 amplitudes) divided by the measured lifetime, i.e. only semi-experimental. For 680 and 1539 nm the same product was formed here (flagged derived). reduced_matrix_element_au (extra field, units e*a0): convention A_ki = omega^3 |<i||er||k>|^2 / (3 pi eps0 hbar c^3 (2J_k+1)), with k the upper level. Values with method 'theory' are CI+MBPT results of Porsev et al. 1999 (accuracy 3-5% for large amplitudes, 15-20% for amplitudes <= 0.5 a.u. and for all amplitudes involving 6s6p 1P1 with singlet partners). oscillator_strength_f (extra field) is stored as printed where a paper gives f rather than A; no f->A conversions were performed in this file. LIFETIMES of 6s6p 3P0 (21.0(18) s) and 3P2 (~8.9 s, theory) are for 171Yb (hyperfine quenching) and do not apply to 174Yb. HYPERFINE: 'hyperfine' holds the adopted value per isotope; 'hyperfine_other' lists competing measurements. 173Yb entries include B (and C where measured). Extra top-level field 'rydberg' holds ionization limits, quantum-defect expansions and excitation routes. Extra level fields: lifetime_other, hyperfine_other, zeeman_171_kHz_per_G (mu_B g_F/h), decay_to_metastable_s, branching_out_of_cycle. Extra transition fields: frequency_other, frequency_components_MHz, wavelength_vac_nm, multipole, oscillator_strength_f, reduced_matrix_element_au(_other), isotope_shift_components_MHz, isotope_shift_direct_MHz, saturation_intensity. Sources read only as abstracts (paywalled full text) are marked 'abstract' in the source string. CONFLICTS: (1) NIST ASD lists A(399 nm) = 1.92e8 s^-1 (Morton 2000), 5% above 1.830(4)e8 s^-1 from the photoassociation lifetime 5.464(5) ns. (2) 399 nm absolute frequency and 1P1 hyperfine constants: Das et al. 2005 / Das-Natarajan 2007 disagree with frequency-comb work (Kleinert 2016, McKnight 2017) by 546 MHz in the 174Yb frequency, ~2 MHz in A(171) and ~7 MHz in B(173); 399 nm isotope shifts in the literature scatter by up to ~3 MHz. (3) 556 nm centres of gravity of 171Yb/173Yb: Atkinson 2019 vs Pandey 2009 differ by 0.5-0.8 MHz. (4) 5d6s 3D1 lifetime: 329.3(7.1) ns (Beloy 2012) vs 380(30) ns (Bowers 1996). (5) 6s7s 3S1 lifetime: 15.9(19) ns (Baumann 1985) vs 12.5(15) ns (Lange 1970); A(171Yb, 3S1): 6837.83(19) (Zhou 2020) vs 6838.69(25) MHz (Qiao 2023). (6) 173Yb 6s6p 3P2: B = 1347.3(9) MHz, C = 0.03(7) MHz (de Groote 2021) vs B = 1339.2(2) MHz, C = 0.54(2) MHz (Singh 2013). (7) 4f13 5d6s2 J=2 lifetime: 5.9(1.3) s inferred in 2023 (lattice-scattering limited) vs 66 s (lower bound 20 s) in 2025. (8) 174Yb ionization limit: 50443.07041(25) (Lehec 2018) vs 50443.07074(4) cm^-1 (Wilson 2022), about 10 MHz apart. (9) The task statement says NIST ASD has no Yb I transition rates; the local Yb_I_lines.tsv does carry five A_ki values (246.5, 267.3, 346.5, 398.9, 555.8 nm lines; Morton 2000), which are copied here where no better value exists.
